entries.title: Living textbook
entries.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: original concept art for a native desktop mathematics game called Paths. This is a newly imagined design, not a capture of an existing application.
Create ONE polished landscape image, roughly 16:10, showing the full application surface edge to edge. No computer, monitor, browser chrome, outer room or presentation board. Crisp high quality UI concept art with readable mathematical typography and precise geometric drawing. Design for an adult learner. Controls and fonts should be compact and practical, with strong hierarchy but no oversized headline. Use short labels, mathematical symbols and numbers. Use the whole height; avoid a large empty band at the bottom.
The product opens like a mathematics textbook, then presents the original problem in one clearly anchored gold-accented band close to the choices. The problem remains fixed while all activity happens in one shared visual workspace. Help stays unobtrusive. Completion waits for an explicit Next. Show carefully authored geometry rather than decorative illustrations, avatars, photographs, unrelated scenery, coins, streak flames or giant dashboard cards.
The consistent accent palette is amber/gold for the original problem or active input, teal for first mathematical object, violet for second, mint for accepted results. Complement colours with distinct shapes or line styles. Precise typography and usable spacing matter more than decorative effects. No watermark. This is a visual design proposal, not an infographic with explanatory arrows outside the UI.
Primary request: Concept 1, the table of contents and question-selection view. This screen feels like a beautifully typeset modern mathematics book made interactive. Warm ivory paper-like surface, graphite typography, faint ruled lines, refined serif chapter names paired with compact sans-serif controls, extremely subtle depth.
Composition: A slim vertical contents column at left, a generous centre column of chapter/problem-type rows, and an integrated mathematical preview on the right. Include enough well-spaced content to fill the height; keep the lower controls attached to the selection list. Use editorial rows, small checkboxes and restrained progress marks rather than a grid of rounded dashboard cards.
Left labels, exactly: "PATHS", "Contents", "Algebra", "Geometry", "Trigonometry", "Calculus". Algebra is selected with an amber marker.
Central chapter title: "Algebra". Show five numbered rows with thin dividers and compact checkboxes: "01  Equations", "02  Inequalities", "03  Functions", "04  Systems", "05  Quadratics". Expand Functions into three indented problem types labelled "Read a graph", "Change a function", "Build a curve", with tiny mathematical forms beside them. The last two chapter checkboxes are visibly selected. A quiet small label "Resume" with "Functions  •  4 / 12" sits near the top of the preview.
The right preview is a clean coordinate drawing of a teal parabola and a violet line, with fine axis labels and a small gold movable point. It is an inviting glimpse of the visual workspace. Under it, a compact two-column values table and a quiet line of three outlined progress dots.
At bottom of selection area use three compact choices "All", "Random", "Select"; selected state "Random", numeric field "12", and a restrained gold-accented "Start set" button. No long prose. Calm, confident, tactile, mathematically literate.

Primary request: Concept 2, the main simultaneous-equations solving workspace. Deep matte charcoal and ink-blue background, exceptionally crisp thin grids, restrained luminous line colours without glow fog. This should look like an elegant technical instrument that is welcoming and easy to operate.
Composition: A narrow top navigation strip with "PATHS", "Algebra / Systems", a small "Resume" indicator and "3 / 12". Beneath it a modest fixed gold-outline problem band showing exactly "y = 2x + 1" and "y = -x + 4". Immediately below, a small prompt "(x, y) = ?" and four compact symbolic choice buttons: "(1, 3)", "(3, 1)", "(0, 4)", "(2, 5)". The math band and choices stay visually close to the large graph.
The graph occupies most of the width and height, with a narrow right rail for a linked values table and earlier working. Use equal-unit x/y axes with origin clearly shown, x spanning -2 to 4 and y spanning -2 to 6. Draw the teal solid line y=2x+1 rising steeply and violet dashed line y=-x+4 falling gently. They cross exactly at (1,3), marked by a small mint ring. White vertical x-guide at x=1 links both points. Label the two lines discreetly with their equations. No decorative curves.
Right table headings "x", "y1", "y2". Rows exactly "0  1  4", "1  3  3", "2  5  2". The middle row has a thin amber outline, with teal and violet values. Below, short retained working: "m1 = 2", "m2 = -1", "N = 1". Keep this rail visually quiet.
A compact x-slider below the graph reads "x = 1.00", with "Replay" near it. A minimal lower edge row contains "Hint", "Show step", and a mint-accented "Next". Preserve ample graph height and usable lower content; no empty bottom region. Subtle bevels are fine, but avoid sci-fi HUD ornaments.

Primary request: Concept 3, a hands-on quadratic construction challenge in the same single workspace. Bright architectural mathematics studio aesthetic: warm off-white, graphite, teal translucent geometry, amber target rings and mint success traces. Refined shallow 3D rendering of mathematical objects with clean flat UI; no physical classroom or desk props.
Top left small title "PATHS", breadcrumb "Algebra / Quadratics". The fixed gold-accented problem strip reads "f(x) = ax² + bx + c". Directly adjacent in smaller type: "(-2, 0)   (0, 4)   (2, 0)" and a short prompt "Pass through all three points".
The dominant central activity is one large shallow-perspective coordinate plane extending through the usable image height. Three small amber ring targets stand on the plane at the exact plotted coordinates (-2,0), (0,4), (2,0). A smooth teal inverted parabola f(x)=4-x² passes precisely through all three; its vertex is at (0,4). Use readable axis labels and sparse fine grid lines. Give the curve a lightly extruded glass-like depth, and the points subtle raised handles, so the player feels able to grasp the maths. Mathematical coherence matters: no random extra arcs or disconnected targets. Mint highlights mark the three successful contacts.
Three small parameter controls labelled "a", "b", "c" sit together immediately below the equation band, values "-1", "0", "4". Each has a narrow slider or paired minus/plus controls. A compact counter "3 / 3" appears near the graph edge. A narrow integrated side strip shows a tiny linked x/f(x) table with rows "-2  0", "0  4", "2  0" and a small saved-progress check.
At the bottom edge of the activity, compact buttons "Reset", "Check", "Next". The UI should express a mathematical game about making something satisfy constraints, with the graph as the thing being played. Mature, tactile, sparse and beautiful; no arcade obstacles, mascots, landscape or giant buttons.

Primary request: Concept 4, a future geometry/calculus activity showing an actual 3D cross-section. Dark graphite workbench with a spacious softly lit mathematical stage, teal wireframe/glass sphere, amber slicing plane, violet cross-section curve. It should feel like a precise interactive mathematical object, not a science-fiction control room.
Top navigation: "PATHS", "Geometry / Cross-sections", compact "5 / 12".
Fixed gold-outline problem band, readable and close to the controls, shows exactly "x² + y² + z² = 9" and "z = 1". Under it the compact prompt "A(1) = ?".
One large central 3D sphere of radius 3, translucent with fine teal latitude/longitude lines, on sparse x/y/z axes. A thin horizontal amber plane cuts the sphere one unit above its centre, creating a violet circular intersection of radius sqrt(8). Show depth clearly with selective occlusion and soft restrained shading. The mathematical object fills the main area; there is no unrelated environment.
At the right of this same activity space, a compact linked flat projection of the circular cross-section with a violet radius line marked "√8". Under it a small numeric table: headings "z", "r²", "A"; rows "0  9  9π", "1  8  8π", "2  5  5π". Outline the middle row in amber. This is a small integrated secondary view, never a separate window or modal.
Directly below the 3D object a compact slicing slider reads "z = 1.00". Four small answer buttons read "5π", "6π", "8π", "9π"; "8π" has a mint outline. "Hint", "Replay" and "Next" sit unobtrusively at the lower edge. Keep the original problem stable and all manipulation on one stage. High visual clarity, subtle volume, clean typography; no bloom, particles, decorative gibberish, giant labels or unused bottom space.

correction.prompt:
Edit this generated Paths graph-workbench concept image. Make ONE targeted correction: fix the two plotted line positions and their coloured point markers so they match the equations and meet at the marked solution. Preserve the typography, layout, dark palette, gold problem band, choice buttons, right-hand table, existing axes and grid, lower controls and all other image content.
The existing image is 1536 by 1024. Use the EXISTING labelled axes in the main plot; do not invent a new graph.
The solid teal line is y = 2x + 1. It must cross the y-axis precisely at y=1, pass through x=1,y=3, and x=2,y=5. Approximately in image pixels: (415,601), (595,467), (770,334); extend it as a single perfectly straight line from around (162,801) to (858,266), clipped at the plot boundary. Put its small teal y-intercept dot at (415,601).
The violet dashed line is y = -x + 4. It must cross the y-axis precisely at y=4, pass through x=1,y=3 and x=2,y=2, and reach x=4,y=0. Approximately in image pixels: (75,266), (415,400), (595,467), (770,534), (1120,668), all on one straight descending dashed line. Put its small violet y-intercept dot at (415,400).
Both coloured lines must meet at exactly one shared mint ring centered approximately (595,467), at x=1 and y=3, directly on the white vertical guide. The ring must surround both crossing lines. Keep the existing labels near their corresponding lines, without overlapping the crossing. Remove the old mispositioned lines and dots rather than leaving duplicates. This remains a visual concept mockup. Do not change any other UI area.
correction.note: One targeted edit attempted to align the lines with the marked solution; geometry remains illustrative and is not a validated mathematical diagram.
